# Relax default `protected_namespaces` config setting (remove `model_`)

Taking inspiration from https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7031, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/9177, and lots of other user feedback, we've decided to relax restrictions on the [`protected_namespaces`](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/api/config/#pydantic.config.ConfigDict.protected_namespaces) config setting.

Many users have reported the fact that it's frustrating to get warnings whenever `model_` is used as a field prefix. This is especially prevalent in AI/ML contexts - it's frequent to have fields like `model_id`, etc.

For reference, this is the current behavior:

```py

from pydantic import BaseModel

class Model(BaseModel):
    model_id: str

"""
UserWarning: Field "model_id" in Model has conflict with protected namespace "model_".

You may be able to resolve this warning by setting `model_config['protected_namespaces'] = ()`.
"""
```

We think the best way forward is to change the default `protected_namespaces` to an empty tuple, rather than the current default, which is `('model_', )`

As noted in #9177, setting `protected_namespaces=()` - which will be the new default, removes errors associated with collisions against pydantic fields (like `model_fields_set` or similar).

So, with `protected_namespaces=('model_',)`, we get a `NameError`:

```py

from pydantic import BaseModel

class Model(BaseModel):
    model_dump: dict

"""
NameError: Field "model_dump" conflicts with member <function BaseModel.model_dump at 0x10360c5e0> of protected namespace "model_".
"""
```

And with `protected_namespaces=()`, we get a `UserWarning`:

```py

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(protected_namespaces=())
    model_dump: dict

"""
UserWarning: Field name "model_dump" in "Model" shadows an attribute in parent "BaseModel"
"""
```

It's still up for debate whether or not this behavior should occur.

We're looking to get some feedback from the community on this change before we implement it.
